correctness.rationale: Eight-vertex circuit normalization is invertible for all positive weights. The four exact crosspolytope-membership inequalities exhaust six/eight-vertex cases; supporting hyperplanes show the only possible quadrilateral faces arise from three signed affine equations. For zero or one equation the McMullen connected-triangle criterion proves indecomposability. For two equations an exact octahedron-plus-segment identity proves decomposability, and the two triangular components and their four cross-edges bound the summand-cone dimension by two. All three equations give a parallelotope. Exact rational supporting-facet computations and edge-deformation ranks independently corroborate the algebraic chamber analysis; these finite checks are not used to infer the universal result.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete, all-positive-parameter classification of the minimal decomposable graph-family example K_{2,2}. It isolates three codimension-two weight strata, separates isolated quadrilateral-facet transitions from actual decomposability, gives an exact nontrivial geometric factorization, and computes the entire 2-ray Minkowski summand cone on each nonuniform decomposable stratum. Those structural distinctions are not mere normalizations of the unit-weight case.
